label: DESIGN-E
files_viewed: DETAIL-desktop.png (full + native-resolution crops of every 900px band)
INTERACTION-desktop.png (full + native-resolution crops of every 900px band)
per_surface_notes: ENTRY: header (logo, 3-icon theme toggle, one black 'Skills' pill), centred hero (author badge, H1, one-line subtitle, single black CTA 'Explorar skills'), two card sections 'Projeto'/'Skills', footer. DISCOVERY: same header ('Home' pill), H1 'Skills', intro + inline hint 'Abra uma skill para o comando de install ou o download', three cards, footer. DETAIL: '← Skills' back link, mono title, INSTALL box (read-only command field + outlined Copy + black 'Download .zip'), long markdown doc with tables and a markdown checklist, 'Licença MIT', footer. INTERACTION: '← Início', title, INSTALL box, progress card '0/54 itens · 0%' with outlined 'Exportar relatório'/'Reiniciar', bar and note 'O progresso fica salvo neste navegador…', then 9 category sections each with counter (0/5…) and bar, 54 checkbox items with title + description, 'ref:' line per section. No mobile hamburger exists (mobile-nav-open captures are identical to first-screens); nav is visible on 390. No data-entry form exists (no form-submit-empty capture); no checked/clicked/after-reset state was captured. Fonts fell back to system sans; not penalised.

verdicts.reason: ENTRY and DISCOVERY use a conventional top bar (logo left, nav pill right), centred hero with H1 + subtitle + single CTA, stacked link cards with trailing arrows, and a standard footer; the only novelty is the three-icon theme switcher, which is small and purposeful.

On ENTRY the black filled 'Explorar skills' button centred under the H1 is immediately identifiable as the single primary action; the header 'Skills' pill uses the same black fill but is small and in the nav corner so it does not compete. DETAIL/INTERACTION likewise have one filled button ('Download .zip') with Copy/Exportar/Reiniciar outlined as secondary.
verdicts.measured_value: 1 filled hero CTA + 1 small filled nav pill

verdicts.reason: Reading order is numberable from size/weight/position alone: ENTRY H1 'Compound Design' (largest, bold, centred) → grey subtitle → black CTA → section headings → cards. INTERACTION: bold page title → grey lead → INSTALL box → progress card → section headings with counters → items.

Related items sit closer than unrelated ones: each card holds its title and description tightly bordered; the INSTALL box groups the command field, Copy and Download; checklist items cluster under their category heading with the 'ref:' line hugging the group, and a large gap separates the next category.

The hero block (badge, H1, subtitle, CTA) is surrounded by roughly 100px of empty space above and below on ENTRY and DISCOVERY, while the card lists and checklist items below are packed with ~12–16px gaps, so whitespace scales with importance.

The action colour is the solid black fill, used only on buttons (hero CTA, nav pill, 'Download .zip'); the only chromatic elements are the small orange dot in the 'In Progress…' status badge and the tiny tri-colour dot in the author badge, neither decorating text or backgrounds.

Colours read as a system: near-black text and filled buttons, two or three greys for secondary text, borders, code chips and the INSTALL box, white surfaces, plus one semantic orange for the 'In Progress' status; no stray hues appear across the four surfaces.

Inline icons (sun, moon, monitor in the theme switcher, the wand logo, the card arrows) are all thin single-weight outline glyphs at the same optical size; the back links use a text '←' glyph, which visually matches the thin card arrows.

Every state indicator present carries text or shape beyond colour: the 'In Progress…' badge pairs its orange dot with a label, progress is shown as '0/54 itens · 0%' and '0/5' counters next to the bars, and the focus state is a thick black outline box around the logo (state-ENTRY-focus-first.png), not a colour change alone.
Content volume is small: ENTRY links to 3 cards, DISCOVERY to 3 skills, and the primary nav is a single Home/Skills pill, well under ~15 destinations, so search is not called for.

At 390px the navigation stays visible in the header (logo link, theme switcher, 'Skills'/'Home' pill) with no hamburger or gesture; the mobile-nav-open captures are identical to the first screens, confirming nothing is hidden, and the wrapped two-line logo does not overflow the viewport.
verdicts.measured_value: nav pill ~32px tall, visible on every mobile surface

verdicts.reason: ENTRY and DISCOVERY disclose progressively (summary card → detail page), but INTERACTION shows all 54 checklist items with their full description and 'ref:' lines expanded at once on a 6709px page with no collapsible sections or on-demand detail. DETAIL likewise renders the whole skill document at once, though that is a reading doc.
verdicts.measured_value: 54 items × title+description always expanded in 9 sections, no collapse/expand control, page height 6709px
verdicts.expected_value: complexity revealed summary → detail (collapsible sections or descriptions on demand)

verdicts.reason: INTERACTION has actions (54 checkboxes, Copy, Exportar relatório, Reiniciar) but no post-click state was captured: all checkboxes are unchecked and no toast, checked state or updated counter is shown, so immediate feedback cannot be verified.
All content is static pages; the only operations are clipboard copy, a markdown export and a .zip download, none long enough to need a designed loading state.

There is no data-entry form: the INSTALL command field is a read-only display beside a Copy button and the checklist is only checkboxes, so inline validation does not apply (no form-submit-empty capture exists).

'Reiniciar' in the progress card is destructive (clears saved progress) but no capture shows what happens after clicking it, so the presence of a confirmation or undo cannot be verified from the screenshots.

ENTRY's first screen states what the site is in one line and puts the 'Explorar skills' CTA and the first project cards inside the 1440×900 fold; INTERACTION's first screen already shows the install command, the progress card and the first checklist section, so the core content is reached without extra steps.

The fresh zero-progress state ('0/54 itens · 0%') is explained in place — 'O progresso fica salvo neste navegador. Exportar copia um relatório em markdown.' — and the page lead tells the user the next step ('marque item a item aqui no navegador'), with the checklist starting directly below.

Help appears at the point of use rather than as a tour: every checklist item carries a one-line explanation under its title and each section ends with a 'ref:' pointer, the progress card has an inline note about saving/exporting, and DISCOVERY tells the user 'Abra uma skill para o comando de install ou o download' right above the cards.
The 54-item audit checklist shows position and remaining work: an overall '0/54 itens · 0%' counter with a progress bar plus per-category counters (0/5, 0/7, 0/9…) each with their own bar.
No testimonials or quotes appear on any of the four surfaces.
No numbers are used as proof; the only figures visible are the checklist counters (0/54), the version string v3.6.0 and the © 2026 footer.

The adoption decision point is the INSTALL box ('npx skills add …', Copy, 'Download .zip') on DETAIL and INTERACTION, and no social proof sits next to it — no stars, user counts, logos or ratings; the only trust text is 'Licença MIT' at the very bottom and 'Inspirado pela comunidade…' in DISCOVERY's footer.
verdicts.measured_value: INSTALL box with no adjacent social proof; 'Licença MIT' ~4000px below
verdicts.expected_value: social proof (logos/badges/ratings) beside the install/download decision

verdicts.reason: No surface collects user data: there is no signup, payment or contact form; the only persisted state is the checklist, which the page explicitly says is saved locally in the browser.
There is no data-entry form to submit — only a read-only install command field with a Copy button and a checklist of checkboxes — so inline error messages do not apply.
No form with multiple input fields exists on any surface; the single visible text field is a read-only command display.
There is no form submission on any surface; Copy, Exportar relatório and Download .zip are not form submits and no submit button is present.
